questions.question_english:
48. Arrange the following United Nations global summits in chronological order:
I. Rio Earth Summit
II. Millennium Summit (MDGs adopted)
III. World Summit on Sustainable Development
(Johannesburg)
IV. UN Conference on Sustainable Development
(Rio+20)
questions.explanation_english: The major United Nations global development summits followed a distinct historic sequence over several decades. The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, known as the Rio Earth Summit, occurred in 1992. The Millennium Summit, where the Millennium Development Goals were adopted, took place in 2000. This was followed by the World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg in 2002, and the UN Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) in 2012.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। संयुक्त राष्ट्र के प्रमुख वैश्विक विकास शिखर सम्मेलन कई दशकों में एक विशिष्ट ऐतिहासिक क्रम का पालन करते हैं। संयुक्त राष्ट्र पर्यावरण और विकास सम्मेलन, जिसे रियो अर्थ समिट के नाम से जाना जाता है, 1992 में हुआ। सहस्त्राब्दी शिखर सम्मेलन, जहाँ सहस्त्राब्दी विकास लक्ष्यों को अपनाया गया, 2000 में हुआ। इसके बाद 2002 में जोहान्सबर्ग में सतत विकास पर विश्व शिखर सम्मेलन हुआ, और 2012 में सतत विकास पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र सम्मेलन (रियो+20) हुआ।

questions.question_english:
90. Consider the following statements regarding the
carbon market mechanisms of the Paris Agreement:
A. Article 6.2 allows for bilateral and multilateral
transfer of mitigation outcomes between countries.
B. Article 6.4 establishes a global carbon
market mechanism overseen by a UN body.
C. ITMOs stands for Internationally Transferred
Mitigation Outcomes.
D. Article 6 completely prohibits developing
countries from participating in carbon trading.
Which of the statements above are correct?
questions.explanation_english:
Article 6 of the Paris Agreement outlines rules
for international carbon trading and market
mechanisms. Article 6.2 enables bilateral
and multilateral transfers of Internationally
Transferred Mitigation Outcomes between
countries, while Article 6.4 creates a global
carbon market under UN supervision. Developing
countries are fully permitted to participate in
